amendments.change: invariants_ref: factory/invariants/seating.yaml added to bean-006, bean-007, bean-009, bean-013
amendments.by: Claude Opus 5 (outside builder), at the owner's direction
amendments.rule: An amendment that only ADDS an independent check does not re-open approval: it narrows what the line may get away with and cannot widen it. An amendment that loosened an acceptance criterion, widened allowed_write_paths, or removed a dependency would re-open it, because those change what a human agreed the line could do.
amendments.note: The invariants were authored before any implementation existed, by a different model family from the developer, and live at a tier-3 path the developer cannot write. They are not human-reviewed; seating.yaml records that plainly under reviewed_by: null.

amendments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (outside builder), at the owner's direction after reviewing seating-planner-py PR #5
amendments.rule: Adds an independent check and loosens nothing: ac2 already said every mutation, and a removal is one. It makes explicit what PR #5 showed the text left open.

The hidden suite gained test_the_audit_log_can_record_a_removal the same day. Not addressed here: PR #5 also logged every unchanged entity as an upsert on each save.

approval_order: bean id order (001..020), which is a valid topological order: every bean's dependencies carry a lower order. Checked, not assumed.
stack_rationale: Implementation Guardrail #2 names OR-Tools CP-SAT, which is Python-native.
FR-048 (identical inputs produce identical assignments) is straightforward to
verify with CP-SAT's seed/worker configuration and hard to verify against a
black-box heuristic. The gate manifest template (ruff / mypy / pytest) applies
unchanged. A TypeScript arm is a later bean set, not a later bean.
ordering_rationale: beans 001-004 scaffold an empty repo and therefore contain nothing: there is no
existing code for allowed_write_paths to protect. Every bean from 005 onward
modifies what an earlier bean wrote, so real callers, real read paths and real
regression risk exist from the fifth bean rather than the twentieth.
bean-019 is a pure refactor (behaviour must not change) and bean-020 is a
correctness fix to code earlier beans are expected to get wrong — both exist to
exercise judgement the happy path never reaches.

scope_exclusions.reason: No verify a gate container can run. Under spec §05 these become `manual` acceptance criteria, and a manual AC forces human review of its bean — which defeats the lights-out goal for every bean carrying one. Excluded from the bean set and recorded here rather than silently dropped or falsely marked auto-verified.
scope_exclusions.revisit: When a browser-driver gate exists, NFR-010 becomes verifiable via axe-core in the gate container.

scope_exclusions.reason: UI surface. v1 is the engine and its data model — the layer where every acceptance criterion is machine-verifiable. A UI bean set is a separate arm of the benchmark, and keeping it separate is what makes the engine results readable.
scope_exclusions.revisit: bean set v2 or a ts-react stack arm.

scope_exclusions.reason: Deployment and operations properties, not properties of the code under test in a disposable benchmark repo.
scope_exclusions.revisit: Out of scope for the corpus permanently.

assumptions.assumed: No. Shared access only; last write wins, with the FR-003 audit record as the reconciliation trail.
assumptions.rationale: Narrowest defensible reading. Real-time collaboration would dominate the architecture and has no bearing on the seating engine the benchmark measures.

assumptions.assumed: Relative canvas coordinates as floats on an arbitrary unit plane, not scaled physical measurements.
assumptions.rationale: FR-014 (proximity between tables) and FR-035 (minimum distance) are both well-defined on any consistent coordinate system. Physical scaling adds a units concern without changing a single acceptance criterion.

assumptions.assumed: No. Table-level assignment only for v1; seat-level layout is deferred.
assumptions.rationale: FR-012 explicitly anticipates unconfigured seats and requires adjacent-seat rules to be reported unevaluable in that state — the PRD itself sanctions deferring it. This is also the largest single scope reduction available, and it creates bean-020: a correctness fix against code written before seats existed.

assumptions.decision: §18.4 — separate permission for private conflict notes
assumptions.assumed: No. Editor access is sufficient to read private notes in v1.
assumptions.rationale: FR-027 and FR-084 constrain where notes may appear (guest-facing screens, exports), which is the property under test. A fourth role changes the permission matrix without changing that property.

assumptions.assumed: 500 guests, 60 tables, 5000 active rules per event.
assumptions.rationale: Comfortably above NFR-001's 250/30/2000 performance target, so the limit never masks the performance criterion. Needed as a concrete bound for validation tests.

assumptions.assumed: Out of scope; no deletion/retention beans in v1.
assumptions.rationale: An operations decision about production infrastructure, unverifiable in a disposable repo.

assumptions.decision: §18.7 — natural-language rule assistant in the first release
assumptions.rationale: Guardrail #8 already makes any LLM-generated rule a draft pending user approval, so the assistant is additive to a structured-rule core that must exist regardless. Excluding it keeps the benchmark's own engine deterministic, which matters because the line building it is not.

assumptions.assumed: Wedding-specific. Domain language is weddings throughout.
assumptions.rationale: FR-028/029 (a default wedding-rule template) are concrete requirements; generalising to arbitrary seated events would make them abstract and less testable.

conflicts_found.description: FR-043 says the system generates assignments for 'all eligible guests'; FR-019 says only Confirmed guests are assigned automatically unless a seat is explicitly reserved for a Pending guest. §5 defines 'eligible guest' consistently with FR-019, so this reads as a wording overlap rather than a contradiction.
conflicts_found.resolution: Treated as consistent: eligible = Confirmed, plus Pending guests with an explicitly reserved seat. Recorded because a bean author could reasonably read FR-043 alone and assign Pending guests.

conflicts_found.description: FR-065 makes the movement limit a hard constraint and FR-047 makes capacity a hard constraint in every mode. A low-disruption run can therefore be infeasible for two different structural reasons, and FR-050/051 must distinguish them in the conflict report or the corrective advice will be wrong.
conflicts_found.resolution: bean-013 requires the infeasibility report to name which hard constraint class caused the failure.

conflicts_found.description: Reproducibility (identical assignment for identical input) and a 15-second bound on 250 guests / 2000 rules can pull against each other: CP-SAT is deterministic per seed only when worker count is fixed, and fixing workers to 1 costs wall-clock.
conflicts_found.resolution: bean-009 pins the solver configuration (including worker count) as persisted data, and NFR-001 is verified against that pinned configuration. If the two prove genuinely incompatible on real data it is an owner decision, not a bean-author decision.
